h: Rookie Tips for Your First Few Laps
p: Never sat in a kart before? Don't sweat it. The quickest way to improve is to look further ahead. Karts tend to go where your eyes go, so instead of staring at the bumper in front, look through the corner to where you want to come out.

Brake in a straight line before the bend rather than halfway round it, then squeeze the power back on gently as you straighten up. Stamping on both pedals at once is the classic beginner's mistake, and it costs more time than you'd think.
Grip the wheel firmly but not like you're strangling it, and sit right back in the seat. Your arms will thank you by the end of the session.
Most of all, enjoy it. Nobody remembers their lap times a week later, but they'll remember the overtakes and the banter.

Afterwards, Gunnersbury Park, on the Acton and Ealing border, is a big green space with a free museum in its old mansion, ideal for winding down. Acton is well served by the Central line and the Elizabeth line, so getting there without a car is easy enough.
